todos.title: Get NetVendor Certified
todos.description: Required by Greystar and other large property management companies before you can pitch. Email compliance@netvendor.net or call 503-922-1111 (option 5). Need: LLC docs, EIN, insurance cert, W-9.
todos.notes: NetVendor certification is a gatekeeper for Greystar and other large PMCs. Get this done ASAP.

todos.title: Call Henderson Business License (702-267-1730)
todos.description: Ask about current classification and per-machine fees. Frame business as "food and beverage distribution to commercial locations using automated dispensing equipment." Check if reclassification is needed.
todos.notes: ✅ DONE — Submitted tonight. Key: registered as food & beverage distribution, NOT vending machine operator. Per Jan 2026 office hours: some cities charge per-machine fees that destroy profitability. Research how Canteen/Aramark register locally and copy their structure.

todos.title: Call Clark County Business License (702-455-4252)
todos.description: Apply for separate license for machines outside Henderson. Register as wholesale/distributor, NOT vending machine operator. Describe as "automated food and beverage distribution."
todos.notes: Separate license needed for any location outside Henderson city limits.

todos.title: Order from VenMarket (triggers USG rebate enrollment)
todos.description: ONE order triggers USG enrollment. Q1 2026 cutoff is March 10. Rebates are 7-13% back on everything. Frito-Lay alone: 11% rebate for 14 items + 0.5% data reporting + 1.5% innovation cases = up to 13%. USG takes 10% admin fee. Net effective COGS 7-10% below VenMarket list. Pro tip: use VenMarket price as COGS in software, treat rebate check as bonus income. Linda from USG audits quarterly.
todos.notes: ⚡ TIME SENSITIVE — Q1 2026 enrollment cutoff is March 10. Just one order kicks off enrollment. Also: VenMarket 1.75oz chip bags = $2.24 profit vs Sam's 1oz bags = $0.87 profit (2.5x more). Bigger bags, higher price points, better perceived value. 5,000+ SKUs available.

todos.title: Build Proposal PDF
todos.description: Professional PDF for property managers to forward to regional (the ACTUAL decision maker). Must include: machine photos, $54/unit rent premium stat (Graystar study — 200 units = $10,800/mo extra rent for property), revenue share tiers (3%/5%/7%/10%), "zero cost to property," 6-month trial period, comparison vs dirty Canteen machines. Use Canva or Zach Iniguez's community proposal builder tools. Get proposals back within 24 hours of every meeting — this is a key differentiator.
todos.notes: The on-site PM is NOT the decision maker. The regional PM makes the call. Give on-site PM a polished PDF to pass up the chain. Per community: PMs getting 10+ cold pitches per month — your proposal must stand out. Customize by location type ("residents" for apartments, "employees" for offices).

todos.title: Start Pop-Ins (minimum 5/day)
todos.description: Walk into Henderson luxury apartments (200+ units, single building/high-rise). Three questions: "Do you have vending? Like it? What would you change?" Bring $5 Costco gift bags. Target 4-5 per hour. For properties with existing vending, use replacement script: "What do you like? What would you change? If I fix everything you mentioned, would you give me a shot?" Never say "vending" — say "smart market" or "luxury amenity." Sales cycle is 10-17+ weeks. Follow-up cadence: 3x week 1, weekly after, then biweekly, then monthly.
todos.notes: Pop-ins are THE #1 acquisition channel — 99.9% of locations are closed face-to-face. Don't wait for machines to arrive. Most existing vendors (Canteen, Aramark) provide terrible service, no revenue share, dirty machines — you're already better. PMs are used to being pitched — stand out with gift bags + professionalism. Ask every PM: "What other properties does your company manage?" One location should generate 3-5 referrals.

todos.title: Apply for SNHD Health Permit
todos.description: Required for food/beverage vending in Clark County (~$250-400/year). Need business licenses first. Apply at SNHD Environmental Health, 280 S Decatur Blvd. Phone: 702-759-1258.
todos.notes: Southern Nevada Health District permit — required before you can legally operate machines with food/beverages.

todos.title: Set Up WeVend Payment Processing
todos.description: Saves $1,656/year vs Stripe at $5,300/mo revenue. WeVend/Preva: ~5.5-5.9% flat, NO per-transaction fee. Stripe's $0.30 per-transaction fee kills margins on $3-4 vending sales. AVOID Cantaloupe: long onboarding (~30 days), machines sit idle, aggressive about deducting equipment financing from sales. Sandstar lets you choose your own processor (not locked in). Payment schedule: 365 pays Fridays weekly, Cantaloupe pays Wednesdays weekly, HaHa pays biweekly ($1 fee for faster).
todos.notes: FEES ARE FOREVER COSTS — more important than upfront machine price. At ~$5,300/month: Stripe ≈ $438/month vs WeVend ≈ $300/month. That's $138/month savings = $1,656/year. This compounds as you scale. Set up before machines arrive.

todos.title: Order Sandstar Machine(s)
todos.description: Sandstar: $3,600 starting, $65/mo SaaS, 5yr compressor warranty, supports AMEX, overnight parts, next-day techs. Charlotte-based, AI integration, outdoor-rated. Choose your own card processor (not locked to Cantaloupe like HaHa/365). Alternative: eVending financing (0% down, 0% interest, 90-day deferment) or HaHa (30% down, 6-month payoff, but NO AMEX, higher fees). NOTE: VP building their own machine (Minus 40 hardware + custom VP software) expected 2026 — may be worth waiting for community pricing.
todos.notes: Key insight from research: FEES > UPFRONT COST. Processing fees are forever costs — more important than machine price. Sandstar lets you choose WeVend (~5.5%) vs being locked to Cantaloupe. Also: Intuitivo tested by VendHub (Oct 2025) — high quality but pricier than MicroMart. Finance machines, keep cash for operations (Anthony's #1 regret was paying cash).

todos.title: Create Gift Bags for Pop-Ins
todos.description: $5 each from Costco. Small snack bags as icebreakers for property managers. The #1 recommended pop-in strategy from the community. Buy 20-30 to start.
todos.notes: NEEDED BEFORE POP-INS. Gift bags are the community's #1 proven icebreaker. Lea Vrabelova (Level 8 member): gift bags initiate rapport immediately. Even operators with zero locations use them to build relationships with PMs. Buy 20-30 from Costco this week.

todos.title: Set Up Vistar Account + Build Relationship
todos.description: Have your Vistar account executive take you to lunch (even with zero locations). Do will-call pickups to build face-to-face rapport with customer service manager. VenMarket + Vistar account = automatic USG rebates (quarterly). VendHub handles resale license uploads (no need to send separately). Off-platform order detection now available (Jan 2026) — auto-detects Vistar orders made outside VenHub. NOTE: Pepsi/Coke bottlers won't deliver to residential — need commercial address (storage unit, partner's business, relative's office works). Vistar is flexible (will meet at nearby Walmart for pickup).
todos.notes: Personal relationships with distributors = better pricing, priority service, rush orders, and flexibility. Build this relationship NOW even before machines arrive. Multiple supply sources: VenMarket, Vistar, Costco, Sam's Club, Walmart, Amazon. Central warehouse improves efficiency (needed around ~12 machines).

todos.title: Get Hartford Workers Comp Quote
todos.description: Some luxury apartments require workers comp even for sole operators. Hub International policy ($1,304/yr) covers GL but may need WC added. Call Hub to ask about adding it.
todos.notes: ✅ DONE — Hub International $1,304/yr for GL + umbrella. Per 2025 master: GL = third-party injury/property (NOT machines). Inland Marine = machines in transit. Scheduled Property = fixed machines (lower rates). Cyber add-on only $25-$50/year. Some states require WC even for 1099 contractors (CA, IL — not NV currently). Luxury apartments in Henderson will likely require WC cert for stockers.

todos.title: Use Clark County Jurisdiction Locator
todos.description: Map your target locations to determine which are Henderson vs unincorporated Clark County vs Las Vegas. You need a business license for EACH jurisdiction. Link: maps.clarkcountynv.gov/gismo/apps/jurisdiction/app/index.html
todos.notes: Critical step — you need separate business licenses for each jurisdiction your machines are in.

todos.title: Stock Initial Inventory (Top Sellers)
todos.description: PROVEN TOP SELLERS: Joy Burst mushroom drink (Vegas #1 — can't keep stocked per operator Madison Graves), Smartwater 20oz ($6K/mo at top locations), Celsius Strawberry Passion Fruit, Coke, Diet Coke, Coke Zero, Fairlife Core Power 42g ($7.99 retail), Gatorade Cool Blue, Dr. Pepper, Alani energy drinks. PREMIUM WATER ONLY: BOSS, Fiji, Voss (don't waste facings on $1-2 water). SNACKS: 1.75oz chip bags from VenMarket (NOT 1oz from Sam's), King-size candy, 5oz gummies, Barebells bars (cookies & cream), Quest chips, Miss Vicky's. INCIDENTALS (secret weapon): Charmin 6-pack ($8→$16.99), Advil 4-pack ($0.50→$3-4, 600-800% markup), phone chargers ($2→$15), Tide Pods, condoms, shampoo. FRESH: Buldak Spicy Carbonara ramen ($1.50→$4), sandwiches at $7-8.
todos.notes: Product mix target: 65% drinks, 30% snacks, 2.5% fresh food, 2.5% incidentals. Target COGS: 31-35%, gross margins: 60-65%. Pricing: convenience store + 10-20% premium. Use $3.95 not $4.00 (pricing psychology). 20oz bottles at $3.00 = floor, not ceiling. Assess mix every 1-2 weeks, kill bottom 5 sellers in first 30 days. Each building has its own personality. Hot climate advantage: extra water inventory (10+ slots), electrolyte drinks.

todos.title: Set Up CRM (HubSpot Free)
todos.description: Free for up to 2 users. Track all prospects, pop-in dates, follow-ups, pipeline stages. Import initial Henderson apartment leads after vetting. Or use Apollo for free multi-step email sequences.
todos.notes: ✅ DONE — Custom dashboard built at vend.kandedash.com with todo tracking, route planner, and business tools. Per community: HubSpot (free/2 users) and Apollo (free email sequences) also recommended. ZoomInfo for property manager data. Simple systems > complex CRMs early on. Track all pop-ins, follow-up dates, pipeline stages.

todos.title: Register for Sales Tax Permit
todos.description: NV Dept of Taxation. Free to register. Required to collect 8.375% sales tax in Clark County. Apply at tax.nv.gov. Phone: 866-962-3707.
todos.notes: ✅ DONE — Permit #SUT-0000-3639-3016. Clark County sales tax rate is 8.375%. Next: file sales tax exemption certificates with Sam's Club, Costco, and Vistar to avoid paying sales tax on wholesale purchases (per Jan 2026 office hours).

todos.title: Set Up Google Voice Number
todos.description: Never use personal phone for business. Google Voice is free. Use this on all flyers, proposals, and business cards. Community strongly recommends this.
todos.notes: NEEDED BEFORE POP-INS START. Never use personal or employer-tied phone numbers for business (strong community consensus). Put this number on all flyers, proposals, business cards, and property contacts.

todos.title: Research Freezer Options for Phase 2
todos.description: Every platform releasing AI freezers H1 2026: HaHa (released), 365 (released), MicroMart (Q1), SandStar (Q2). Minus 40 freezers = best in class for reliability/aesthetics. Nestle/Mars incentive: 6 Nestle + 4 Mars items = free cases or pusher kits (up to 5 freezers/operator). Use AMPS framework: Assortment (strong brands), Merchandising (clean presentation), Pricing (total freezer margin, not per-item), Shelving (ice cream at eye level, big items at bottom). Dual-temperature option (half cooler/half freezer) for space-constrained locations.
todos.notes: Phase 2 opportunity. Frozen meals: Eat Fit Go ($12-$15, 14-day refrigerated / 6-month frozen shelf life, order Fri 3pm CT → ships Mon). Factor meals: fresh, 7-day shelf life. Frozen microwavable preferred (longer shelf life, less spoilage). Vistar has a freezer planogram calculator (Excel). Pico Freezer Vision solved camera fogging after 50+ iterations.

todos.title: Explore PrintWithMe Coffee Partnership
todos.description: Caffection Cymbal machine: 12 drink options, resident allowances (5-30 cups/month). Cross-sell opportunity during property pop-ins. Can reduce PM's coffee spend by 60%.
todos.notes: Great cross-sell during pop-ins. Reduces property coffee spend by 60%.

todos.title: Build Route Plan (First 5 Locations)
todos.description: Use the Route Planner on dashboard. Keep all locations within 30-35 min of West Henderson base. Optimize for Tier 1 areas first (Henderson, Green Valley, Seven Hills).
todos.notes: Use /route-planner page. Tier 1 areas: Henderson, Green Valley, Seven Hills.

todos.title: Finish Clark County Business License Application
todos.description: Resume app ID xt2wwv at blepay.clarkcountynv.gov. Fill owner info (Kurtis CEO 50%, Elaine Owner 50%), complete remaining steps. Register as wholesale distributor to avoid per-machine fees.

todos.title: File Sales Tax Exemption Certificates with Distributors
todos.description: Now that sales tax permit (SUT-0000-3639-3016) is active, file exemption certificates with Sam's Club, Costco, and Vistar so you don't pay sales tax on wholesale purchases for resale. Per Jan 2026 office hours: this is a standard step most operators miss early on. VendHub handles Vistar resale license uploads automatically.
todos.notes: You're losing money on every wholesale purchase until these are filed. Sales tax on COGS eats into your 60-65% target margins.

todos.title: Create One-Page Contract Template
todos.description: Simple one-page service agreement (NEVER say "contract"). Include: 6-month trial period, machine specs, revenue share tiers (only if they ask), relocation clause for underperforming locations, zero cost to property. Use clawback clauses ONLY for large multi-location investments ($25K+). For single machine placements, keep it simple — no scary legal language. 12-24 month minimum commitment as alternative to clawbacks.
todos.notes: Per community: trial periods overcome hesitancy. Never use the word "contract" — say "service agreement." Revenue share on GROSS revenue only (properties don't trust net). Tiered: 3% ($800-$1,600), 5% ($1,600-$2,500), 7% ($2,500-$4,000), 10% ($4,000+). Payments quarterly. If they don't ask for rev share — DON'T bring it up.

todos.title: Create Pop-In Flyer (Curiosity-Based)
todos.description: Design a flyer that creates curiosity, NOT one that explains everything. Include: machine photo, "Smart Market" or "Luxury Amenity" branding (never "vending"), QR code to proposal/website, Google Voice number, Kande VendTech logo. Per Skool community: flyers should make PMs want to learn more, not give away all the details. Different from the full proposal PDF — this is the leave-behind.
todos.notes: Use alongside gift bags during pop-ins. This is what you leave when the PM isn't available. Key phrases to include: "smart AI-powered market," "zero cost amenity," "premium convenience." Avoid: "vending machine," "contract," pricing details.

todos.title: Apply for 0% APR Business Credit Cards
todos.description: Business credit cards with 0% APR intro periods (12 months) are a key financing tool for new operators. Recommended: Chase Ink Business, AMEX Blue Business Plus. Also consider Pathfinder 2 Funding (Matt Schultz) for higher-limit approvals (~6% fee). Corporate cards that don't report utilization to personal credit are ideal. Use for inventory, equipment, and early operating expenses.
todos.notes: Per Jan 2026 office hours: many operators "hobble together" financing early — better options come after 2 years of history. Don't liquidate savings/retirement to buy machines (mistake #8 from YouTube research). Finance machines, keep cash for operations. Think 2-3 years ahead before maximizing depreciation (affects mortgage/financing eligibility).

todos.title: Add Inland Marine + Cyber Coverage to Insurance
todos.description: Current Hub International policy ($1,304/yr) covers GL + umbrella. Still need: Inland Marine (covers machines in transit — critical when moving/installing), Scheduled Property (covers fixed/installed machines at lower rates than IM), and Cyber add-on ($25-$50/year — covers payment processing breaches). Also set theft coverage threshold carefully to avoid rate hikes (use crime policy, not GL).
todos.notes: Per 2025 insurance deep dive (Hub International, Aug 2025): GL = third-party injury/property only, NOT your machines. Machine in FL = $200-$400/yr coverage, OR = ~$75/yr. Will need machine serial numbers to add to policy. One VP member had machine stolen from apartment lobby — insurance covered full claim. Bolt machines to floor where possible.

todos.title: Tax Strategy: Stay Single-Member LLC, Set Aside 25-30%
todos.description: Stay as single-member LLC until hitting $70-80K annual PROFITS, then evaluate S-Corp election. S-Corp requires reasonable salary + distributions (distributions avoid FICA tax). IRS is cracking down — NO 50/50 rule exists. Set aside 25-30% of all profits in a separate tax-only savings account. Section 179: 100% machine write-off (can't create a loss). Bonus depreciation: 100% write-off (CAN create a loss). Use Xero (not QuickBooks). Hire local CPA — interview in Dec/Jan, NOT during tax season.
todos.notes: ⚠️ Think 2-3 years ahead before maximizing depreciation — it kills mortgage and financing eligibility. Home office deduction: use "accountable plan" for larger deduction (garage + dedicated rooms). Year-end: must count ALL inventory (warehouse + in machines) for tax purposes. Don't elect S-Corp too early — it adds complexity and costs.

todos.title: Get Placer AI Access for Location Research
todos.description: Placer AI provides real foot traffic data for any address. Critical for evaluating medical facilities, apartment complexes, and warehouses before committing. One operator used it to get 3 years of patient foot traffic data for a medical facility pitch. Also useful for comparing competing locations side-by-side. Use data in proposals: real numbers close deals that promises can't.
todos.notes: Location minimum thresholds: 200+ units (apartments), 150+ employees (manufacturing), 250+ people/day (medical), 100+ people/day (general). Under $500/month per location NOT worth servicing. Under $1,500/month = pull at 90 days.

todos.title: Secure Commercial Address for Bottler Deliveries
todos.description: Pepsi and Coke bottlers will NOT deliver to residential addresses — they verify. Need a commercial address for USG/Pepsi program enrollment (Q1 2026 deadline was Dec 15 for enrollment, but deliveries ongoing). Options: storage unit, partner's business, relative's office, friend's commercial space. Vistar is more flexible (will meet at nearby Walmart for pickup). This is required before scaling to bottler-direct pricing.
todos.notes: Per 2025 master: Pepsi verifies commercial addresses — residential gets rejected. 24-48 hours to fix address issues. Multiple regional bottlers = phased rollout. Deliveries via pallet jacks. This becomes critical when scaling past ~10 machines and Costco/Sam's pricing isn't competitive enough.

todos.title: Target Medical Outpatient Facilities (Phase 2)
todos.description: Medical outpatient = recession-proof gold. 150+ employees, 100+ patients/day, high stress = impulse buying. Frame as employee/patient amenity (revenue share less common in medical). Product mix: Quest chips, Barebells bars, kid-friendly items (applesauce, Sunny D). Include cash acceptance (Moneta) for elderly patients. Approach: HR (employee benefit angle), food services director, or contracting specialists. Use Placer AI for foot traffic verification. Avoid: urgent cares (only 20-25 patients/day), inpatient (requires credentials).
todos.notes: Phase 2 after establishing apartment base. Vegas has major hospital systems (UMC, Sunrise, Valley) with outpatient facilities everywhere. Blue-collar/physical labor environments drive more purchasing than white-collar offices. Consider freezer + drink + ambient vs. full micro-market setup.

todos.title: Set Up Follow-Up Tracking System
todos.description: Deals take 7-17+ visits to close. Build a systematic follow-up cadence in your CRM/dashboard: 3x in week 1 after first pop-in, weekly for 2-3 weeks, biweekly for 1-2 months, monthly after that. NEVER say "just checking in" — bring value each time (snack sample, seasonal note, new data). Neutral touchpoints ("Happy New Year") maintain presence without being pushy. Cold/no-response: follow up in 3 months. Track every interaction.
todos.notes: Follow-up is THE actual business per every top operator. Some clients require 90 days and 7-17+ visits before committing. Operators who follow up win. Period. Biweekly initially → monthly to avoid annoyance. Physical visits more effective than emails. Offer $250 referral fee to PMs for successful sister property introductions.

todos.title: Register on NSHE Supplier Portal
todos.description: Go to https://suppliers.nevada.edu → Register a new account. Required to bid on any CSN/NSHE contract.

todos.title: Call CSN Purchasing — Ask About Vending RFP
todos.description: Call Rolando Mosqueda (702) 651-4245 or Paula Gonzales (702) 651-4039. Ask if there is an active or upcoming vending services RFP. Mention: Henderson-based, smart coolers, cashless, micro market capability.

todos.title: Get Business Insurance (BOP Policy)
todos.description: Get quotes for Business Owner Policy — need $1M GL minimum for state contracts and property manager requirements. ~$50-100/mo. Check Progressive, Hiscox, Next Insurance, Hartford.

todos.title: Apply for Nevada ESB Certification
todos.description: Emerging Small Business certification gives preference on state bids. Free to apply, ~90 day process. Start ASAP. Research requirements in /kande-vendtech/research/ folder.

todos.title: Call APEX Accelerator — Free Gov Contracting Help
todos.description: John Rice: (702) 486-0585. Free advisor for government contracting. Schedule a consultation to get help with NSHE/state bids.

todos.title: Contact Republic Services HQ (Henderson)
todos.description: Score 92. 1K-5K employees at Henderson HQ. Find facilities or vendor procurement contact.

todos.title: File Public Records Request — First Class Vending NDOC Contract
todos.description: Draft FOIA request for First Class Vending Inc NDOC contract details (terms, revenue, expiration). Template in /kande-vendtech/research/foia-request-first-class.md

todos.title: Verify NV Business License & Secretary of State
todos.description: Confirm Kande VendTech LLC is current at nvsos.gov. Needed before any government contracting.

todos.title: Research Henderson Apartment Complexes for Vending
todos.description: Top targets: Elysian at Tivoli, Inspirada apartments, Cadence apartments, The Bend at Seven Hills, Tuscan Highlands. Contact property managers. Details being researched by sub-agent.

todos.title: Call Clark County (702) 455-4252 — download business license. App ID: 7ei1o7

SMART MARKET AMENITY PARTNERSHIP AGREEMENT

Revenue Share Model

Agreement #{{contract_number}}

This Amenity Partnership Agreement ("Agreement") is entered into as of {{start_date}} ("Effective Date") by and between:

AMENITY PARTNER:
Kandé VendTech LLC
Henderson, NV
Phone: {{company_phone}}
Email: {{company_email}}		 PROPERTY:
{{client_name}}
{{property_address}}
Contact: {{contact_name}}
Phone: {{contact_phone}}
Email: {{contact_email}}

1. SCOPE OF SERVICES

Kandé VendTech ("Partner") shall install, stock, maintain, and service {{machine_count}} AI-powered smart market unit(s) at the Property location(s) specified above. Services include:

  • Installation and setup of smart market equipment at zero cost to Property
  • Regular restocking with premium snacks, beverages, and convenience items
  • Ongoing maintenance, cleaning, and technical support
  • Cashless payment processing (credit/debit, mobile pay, tap-to-pay)
  • Remote monitoring and inventory optimization
  • 24/7 customer support via QR code feedback system

2. REVENUE SHARE

Partner shall pay Property a revenue share of {{rev_share_percent}}% of gross sales generated by the smart market unit(s), payable monthly. Revenue share payments shall commence {{rev_share_start}} after installation date.

Estimated monthly revenue: ${{estimated_monthly_revenue}}

3. TERM

This Agreement shall be for an initial term of {{term_years}} years commencing on the Effective Date, with automatic renewal for successive one-year periods unless either party provides written notice of non-renewal at least 60 days prior to the expiration of the then-current term.

4. EQUIPMENT & INSTALLATION

  • All equipment remains the property of Kandé VendTech
  • Installation at zero cost to Property — no upfront fees
  • Property shall provide suitable electrical outlet (standard 110V) and reasonable access
  • Partner responsible for all equipment maintenance and repair

5. PROPERTY OBLIGATIONS

  • Provide suitable, secure indoor location for equipment
  • Maintain adequate electrical supply and climate control
  • Grant reasonable access for restocking and maintenance (minimum 2x per week)
  • Notify Partner promptly of any equipment issues or damage
  • Not install competing snack/beverage amenity services during the term

6. PRODUCT SELECTION

Partner shall stock products based on resident/employee preferences, seasonal trends, and sales data analytics. Property may request specific products or dietary options. Partner will accommodate reasonable requests within 14 days.

7. INSURANCE & LIABILITY

Partner maintains comprehensive general liability insurance of not less than $1,000,000 per occurrence. Partner shall add Property as additional insured upon request. Partner assumes all liability for equipment operation and product quality.

8. TERMINATION

  • Either party may terminate with 60 days written notice after the initial term
  • Early termination by Property during initial term requires 90 days notice
  • Partner may terminate immediately if Property breaches exclusivity clause
  • Upon termination, Partner shall remove equipment within 14 business days

9. ADDITIONAL TERMS

{{additional_terms}}

KANDÉ VENDTECH LLC
